Oriental Insurance Co Ltd., ... vs Lalam Satyavathi,
Visakhapatnam Anr on 12 November, 2024
 The Honourable Sri Justice Nyapathy Vijay
 Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.684 of 2014
Judgment:

entities.text:
Oriental Insurance Co Ltd., ... vs Lalam Satyavathi,
Visakhapatnam Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1. This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed under Section 30 of Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 questioning the Award passed by the Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation and Assistant Commissioner of Labour, Narsipatnam, Visakhapatnam District in W.C.No.24 of 2010, dated 18.07.2012.

2. The facts leading to the present Appeal are, as under:-
One Mr.Venkata Ramana (hereinafter referred to as the deceased) was said to be working as a cleaner-cum-helper under O.P-1/Turbo Lorry bearing No. AP 07 X 8105 and he was paying a monthly salary of Rs.4,000/-.
On 28.07.2007, one Mr.T.Venkateswara Reddy, who is the co-partner of O.P-1 in Veligonda Project contract works, instructed the deceased and driver for shifting of concrete bucket in the lorry.
The said work was belonging to the Principal Contractor L&T, which was executing works for the Veligoda Project.
While shifting of the concrete bucket, the Supervisor of Principal Contractor, L&T, instructed the deceased to stop shifting of the concrete bucket until further instructions from him.
According to the instructions of the Supervisor, the driver of O.P-1 stopped the shifting work and parked the lorry near to the working place for further instructions.
After dinner, the driver of the lorry slept in the cabin and the deceased slept on the side of the lorry of O.P-1.

On the next day, i.e. on 29.07.2007, it was noticed that the husband of the Claimant had died and on enquiry, they came to know that the husband of the Claimant had died due to rash and negligent driving of lorry driver of lorry bearing No. AP7X8105.
3.
The Police, Markapuram Rural Police Station, registered a case in Crime No.59 of 2007 for the offence punishable under Section 304-A I.P.C.
As no compensation was being paid by the O.P-1, an application was filed seeking compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- by the Claimant/wife of the deceased.
4. The O.P-1/Employer has filed his Counter denying the employment of the deceased as cleaner in the said lorry bearing No.AP7X8105 and also the wages paid of Rs.4,000/- per month.

O.P-1 was also denied that T.Venkateswar Reddy as his co-partner, as alleged in the claim application and also the work entrusted to the deceased along with driver of L & T.
5.
O.P-2/Insurance Company also denied any liability.

6. The Commissioner framed the following issues for consideration, which read as under:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1. Whether the deceased is a workman under the provisions of W.C. Act and there exists employee-employer relation and death aroused out of and in the course of employment?
2. What is the Age & Wage of the deceased at the time of the accident?
3. Whether the applicant is entitled for any amount of compensation?

If so, what amount of compensation the applicants are entitled and who are liable to pay compensation?
7.
In the course of enquiry, the Claimant was examined as A.W.1 and marked Exs.A1 to A6, whereas Ex.B1 was marked on behalf of the Insurance Company.

8. After framing the issues, the Commissioner after hearing the respective counsel and the evidence on record, held that the deceased was employed under O.P-1 in view of the attested copy of F.I.R and awarded compensation of Rs. 2,86,510/-.
Aggrieved thereby, the present Appeal is filed.

9. Heard Sri Gudi Srinivas, learned counsel representing the Appellant and no representation on behalf of the Respondents.
10.

After hearing the counsel for the Appellant, the question of law that falls for consideration for this Appeal is as follows:
Whether the Order of the Commissioner in holding that the deceased was an employee of O.P-1 is sustainable?
11.
The critical factor in this case is that Employer/O.P.No.1 had denied employment specifically in his Counter.
Apart from the self-serving oral evidence of the Claimant, there is absolutely no evidence in favour of the Claimant i.e. establishing employment.
The reliance on the F.I.R by the Commissioner is misplaced, as the F.I.R does not establish any employer-employee relationship.
Therefore, this is a case of no evidence and the order of the Commissioner needs to be interfered with.

12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Municipal Committee, Hoshiarpur v. Punjab SEB1 while considering an Appeal under Section 100 CPC held that perverse findings and findings based on no evidence can be interfered even in a Second Appeal.

entities.text: Municipal Committee, Hoshiarpur v. Punjab SEB1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Paragraph 28 thereof is extracted below:

"28. If a finding of fact is arrived at by ignoring or excluding relevant material or by taking into consideration irrelevant material or if the finding so outrageously defies logic as to suffer from the vice of irrationality incurring the blame of being (2010) 13 SCC 216 perverse, then the finding is rendered infirm in the eye of the law.

If the findings of the Court are based on no evidence or evidence which is thoroughly unreliable or evidence that suffers from the vice of procedural irregularity or the findings are such that no Oriental Insurance Co Ltd., ... vs Lalam Satyavathi, Visakhapatnam Anr on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154440902/
2 reasonable person would have arrived at those findings, then the findings may be said to be perverse.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co Ltd., ... vs Lalam Satyavathi, Visakhapatnam Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further if the findings are either ipse dixit of the Court or based on conjecture and surmises, the judgment suffers from the additional infirmity of non- application of mind and thus,
stands vitiated (vide Bharatha Matha v. R. Vijaya Renganathan)."
13.

entities.text: Bharatha Matha v. R. Vijaya Renganathan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The scope of interference even in Appeals under Section 30 of the Workmen's Compensation Act is limited and even if the finding is plausible, the same can be sustained.
However, in this Appeal, as stated supra, there is absolutely no evidence to establish the jurisdictional jural relationship of employee-employer.

14. Result: The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is therefore allowed by setting-aside the Award passed by Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation and Assistant Commissioner of Labour, Narsipatnam in W.C.No.24 of 2010, dated 18.07.2012.
The Claimant is at liberty to file an application for compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, pending applications, if any, shall stand closed.
